about: DRIFT's garden as a film. Each plant in plants.json is a character, set where that plant thrives on Earth and written after a performance from the history of cinema; the protagonist is the coleus, which loves heat and keeps to the shade. In DRIFT each character walks round its plant in its garden, doing what it does in its scene, and the collage glues in its title card (cast.js). Every plant added to plants.json gets a character here (COWORKER.md, step 3a).

cast.name: Plectra
cast.role: the protagonist: a woman of every colour who will not stand in the sun
cast.climate: equatorial rainforest, 25 °C year-round, under the canopy
cast.scene: She crosses every garden in the film and takes on each one's colours as she passes, slowing in the shade, hurrying across the open.
cast.why: Feeling held back in shadowed corridors, every colour kept under the surface (Best Actor, Cannes 2000).

cast.name: Rosa Damascena
cast.role: a perfumer obsessed with a single rose
cast.climate: continental, cold winters, the harvest in May and June
cast.scene: Before sunrise, when the oil is richest, he picks the damask roses by hand, then holds one up against the sky until it hangs there on its own.
cast.why: A maker who arranges the world round one obsession with beauty; the only man with three Best Actor Oscars.

cast.name: Acantha
cast.role: an old master in a wheelchair, cutting leaves out of painted paper
cast.climate: Mediterranean: green in the winter rain, dormant through the dry summer
cast.scene: Among the broken columns, whose capitals Vitruvius says were first carved after an acanthus grown round a basket on a girl's grave, she cuts the living leaf in paper and pins it to the stone.
cast.why: Late life met with fierce dignity (BAFTA and César for Best Actress).

cast.name: Ajisai
cast.role: a dyer who reads colour in the soil
cast.climate: humid subtropical; the plum rains of June
cast.scene: Through the rainy season she pours blue and pink into the ground and waits to see which the flowers drink up.
cast.why: A quiet that holds everything (Tokyo Story topped Sight & Sound's directors' poll in 2012).

cast.name: Selene
cast.role: a street photographer who waits all night
cast.scene: From a balcony he watches a cactus climbing a colonial wall; at midnight it opens for a single night, and he has one exposure.
cast.why: A photographer who watches and waits, all patience and nerve (Best Actor Oscar, The Philadelphia Story).

cast.name: Wallera
cast.role: a painter who cannot be touched
cast.climate: tropical montane cloud forest, mist and moss
cast.scene: In the wet shade he works on the ground; when anyone comes near, everything bursts, as the touch-me-not's pods fling their seeds.
cast.why: Raw, physical, explosive; Best Actor Oscars for On the Waterfront and The Godfather.

cast.name: Rtveli
cast.climate: humid continental; hot summers, the vintage in September
cast.scene: At the harvest in the oldest wine country on Earth (wine made here by 6000 BC) she paints the god among the pickers and will not stop moving.
cast.why: Earthy, unstoppable force (Best Actress Oscar, The Rose Tattoo).

cast.name: Sievers
cast.role: a photographer of light in a wild forest
cast.place: the Tian Shan above Almaty, Kazakhstan
cast.climate: continental mountain; snowy winters, blossom in late April
cast.scene: He walks the wild apple forest where every apple began (Malus sieversii) and photographs the blossom in silence, in black and white.
cast.why: An angel who watches the world in black and white and longs for colour.

cast.name: Bunga Raya
cast.role: a celebrity who runs a factory of copies
cast.climate: tropical rainforest; heat and afternoon storms
cast.scene: Under the national flower he prints the same hibiscus over and over in every colour and never changes expression.
cast.why: The Great Stone Face: deadpan perfection, repeated (honorary Oscar, 1960).

cast.name: May
cast.role: a painter of one lane in every season
cast.scene: Every morning he sets up in the same lane and paints it again; the week the hawthorn opens, the hedges turn white like surf.
cast.why: A Yorkshire-raised luminary lit by landscape (eight nominations, honorary Oscar 2003).

cast.name: Drummond
cast.role: a captain who only sails at dusk
cast.climate: humid subtropical Gulf coast; dunes and storms
cast.scene: As the sun goes down the beach evening primroses open on the dunes; he ties himself to the mast and steers into the storm to see it.
cast.why: Elemental force and weather (the Volpi Cup at Venice twice, for Yojimbo and Red Beard).

cast.name: Rajah
cast.climate: tropical montane cloud forest, cool and wet
cast.scene: She climbs to the giant pitchers in the cloud and looks down into one until its dark has no floor.
cast.performance: The Passion of Joan of Arc
cast.why: A face looked into as into an abyss; her one great screen role, still counted among cinema's greatest.

cast.name: Primula
cast.role: a stubborn painter of the mountain
cast.place: the pines of Château Noir, Provence
cast.climate: Mediterranean heat; the primrose keeps to the cool shade of the pines
cast.scene: Each day he climbs out to paint the mountain again, and sets the primrose in the shade beside him as the one cool thing in the heat.
cast.why: Patient, grave, unyielding: a knight playing chess with Death.

cast.name: Iris Mistral
cast.role: a painter in the garden of an asylum
cast.scene: In his first week in the asylum he paints the irises bed by bed while the mistral bends every one of them.
cast.why: Joy and anguish in the same face (Best Actress, Cannes 1957).

cast.name: Nymphe
cast.climate: temperate oceanic; the pond warmed by summer
cast.scene: Her eyes clouding (Monet's cataract was operated on in 1923), she paints the pond from memory and the colours run together as the water does.
cast.why: Age, love and water (her fourth Best Actress Oscar, the record).
